spec: Which systems cannot run without firmware — the half a libretro .info cannot state. A core declares firmware one file at a time with firmwareN_opt, a format with no way to say 'one of these three' and no way to say 'this system does not start without one of them'. An author who knows a PlayStation needs one regional BIOS therefore has two lossy moves, and the deployed catalogue takes both: Beetle PSX marks scph5500/5501/5502 required and RetroArch then demands all three, SwanStation marks all five of its images optional and RetroArch demands none. atlas reports 'need' straight from firmwareN_opt and so reproduces both faithfully, which over an all-optional PlayStation reads as 'nothing required' about a system that will not boot. This table records the missing half as world knowledge, and it records it about the SYSTEM rather than about the core, because that is where the fact lives: mGBA, snes9x and gambatte declare everything optional and are simply right, while swanstation declares everything optional about a machine that needs a BIOS. Entries are keyed by the libretro 'systemname' string VERBATIM, not by an ES-DE system id, because systemname is the unit the .info catalogue groups firmware by and therefore the unit the tripwire's derivation produces; translating into atlas's own vocabulary is not free ('Game Boy/Game Boy Color' is one systemname over two catalogue systems) and it is a question for the cut that makes an answer carry this table, not for the cut that records it. 'verdict' is one of three: 'cannot-run-without-firmware' (no firmware, no boot), 'runs-without-firmware' (the system starts with none present), and 'open' (nobody has established which). 'open' is a real value and not an absence — it is how a system whose cores disagree leaves the tripwire without anyone pretending to know, and it is why six of the seven entries here exist at all. 'evidence' is the repo's own level for the verdict ([V] verified, [D] derived, [O] open) and is tied to it: an 'open' verdict carries [O] and nothing else carries [O], because a verdict that states something cannot rest on an open question and an open question cannot claim a verified reading. 'source' says what the level rests on, in the marker vocabulary the other tables use ([V-live] an observation on a real machine, [V-binary] a read of the shipped core, [V-script] the arrangement's own scripts). 'cores_supplying_an_alternative' names the cores whose all-optional declaration is CORRECT for a system that needs firmware, because the core itself supplies a way to run without a file — PCSX ReARMed's HLE BIOS is the case this table was written around, and without naming it the tripwire would call a correct catalogue entry a mistake. It appears only on a 'cannot-run-without-firmware' entry, where the question 'is this core understating?' can arise at all, and each core names its own reason rather than being a bare exemption. The list is NOT a completeness claim: it exempts the cores whose alternative has been established, and a core absent from it is a core nobody has looked at, never a core judged to be understating. Today one system carries a verdict. The other six are the disagreements the tripwire in tests/test_system_firmware_tripwire.py derives from the deployed catalogue, recorded as open so that they are visible rather than merely unrecorded, and that tripwire is what keeps this file honest: it recomputes the disagreements at run time and fails when it finds one this file does not carry.

PlayStation.source: [V-live] Observed on a RetroDECK installation with no PlayStation BIOS present: SwanStation never starts, and Beetle PSX refuses at load and names scph5501.bin on screen. [V-binary] Read off the shipped cores: swanstation registers three region BIOS PATH slots (swanstation_BIOS_PathNTSCJ, _PathNTSCU, _PathPAL) whose values are file names only (scph5500.bin / scph5501.bin / scph5502.bin, psxonpsp660.bin, ps1_rom.bin) with no value that stands for 'no file', and beetle_psx_hw's own beetle_psx_hw_override_bios likewise offers only images. [D] The catalogue reproduces the same fact twice and lossily in both directions: mednafen_psx and mednafen_psx_hw declare the three region images required and their two alternates optional, while swanstation, pcsx1, pcsx_rearmed_interpreter and pcsx_rearmed_neon declare every image optional — one machine, one requirement, and a per-file flag that can express neither 'one of these' nor 'none of these will do'.

cores_supplying_an_alternative.pcsx_rearmed: [V-binary] The core registers pcsx_rearmed_bios with the two values 'auto' and 'HLE', which is a way to run with no image on disk at all; every other PlayStation core deployed here offers only a choice between files. [V-live] It was observed starting and playing a game through on a machine with no PlayStation BIOS present. That is the whole of the evidence, and the limit is worth stating: which of the two values was in force during that run is not recorded, and nothing here establishes what 'auto' does when no image is present. The exemption rests on the observation that this core ran without firmware, not on a reading of what either value means.

Saturn.source: [D] The deployed catalogue disagrees with itself: kronos, mednafen_saturn and yabasanshiro each declare a required file, and yabause declares everything optional. [O] Nothing has been observed on a machine and no core option has been read, so whether a Saturn starts with no firmware present is unestablished.

This key is one systemname over two catalogue systems, which is the spec's own reason for keying by systemname rather than by an ES-DE id.
